evidence: Compared DRAFT, “Remind yourself that if you say 'stop' at any time, the induction will end. If you say 'less', you will be asked to do less. If you say 'quiet', the talking will stop.”, with SOURCE.txt word by word (the two replaced sentences and the meaning to keep: “Stop” ends the exercise; “less” reduces the demand; “quiet” stops the words). All three controls are there with the same effects and nothing else is added: 'stop' ends the induction and keeps “at any time” (source: “you can say 'stop' at any time and the induction will end”); 'less' means you will be asked to do less (source: “asking for less from you”; meaning to keep: “reduces the demand”); 'quiet' stops the talking (source: “say 'quiet' and the talking will stop”). No fourth word, condition, person or number appears, and the order is his (stop, less, quiet). Differences I checked and judge within his meaning: (1) “Know that you can say” became “Remind yourself that if you say”: the ability to say stop at any time is carried by the conditional and by “at any time”; “Remind yourself” turns an awareness line into a self-reminder and presupposes the reader has met the words before, but the sentence itself tells what each word does, so no fact is lost or added; (2) “If you want to change something, say 'less' if you want it to be asking for less from you” became a plain consequence (“If you say 'less', you will be asked to do less”): the cue about wanting a change is gone, but it is not in the meaning to keep and each word’s effect is stated; “asked to do less” is slightly narrower in wording than “asking for less from you” but says the same for an induction that asks the reader to do things; (3) the passive “you will be asked” leaves the asker unnamed where the source had “it”, and the asker is plainly the induction, as in the source. CONTEXT holds the draft once, mid-paragraph in “Deciding to do it.”, after “If you are going to use a recording, read the script if you can.” and before “You can also just open your eyes and stop…”, whose “also” still follows naturally; “the induction” is defined above (“during the induction”). CONTEXT also shows the G-S3a pointer in the paragraph above, which does not touch this passage. Tells: T02 UNCERTAIN at paragraph scale, resolved as justified: the draft makes three consecutive compressed conditions in lockstep (the source had two looser sentences) inside a paragraph that is already a run of short prompts, so a cold reader may feel the cadence; but these are three separately actionable safety controls that his own published line also lists as a triple (“Stop” ends…; “less” reduces…; “quiet” stops…), a parallel frame lets the reader find each word and its effect, and the paragraph still carries its noticing lines (“You can also just open your eyes and stop…”, “even if a part tells you that you do”) untouched. T12 considered and judged ABSENT: the set of three is real (his three words), not a taxonomy built for balance. T09 and T13 considered (the linter’s D9 note): the three lines are a rule list with equal weight because the three controls carry equal weight, and the noticing sentences of the paragraph are unchanged by this edit. T22: “Remind yourself that” is the only coach-sounding opener; it is the same register as the replaced “Know that you can say”, and the lines state concrete mechanisms, not reassurance alone, so ABSENT. T15 not present (the structure changed, not just the words). C02: “the talking” means the narration, as in the source. Linter findings: B7 short landing at paragraph end is accepted: the linter saw the draft alone, but in the article “If you say 'quiet', the talking will stop.” is not the paragraph’s end (two more sentences follow) and carries no flourish, just the third control. D9 follows the source order is accepted: the order stop, less, quiet is his own published order and the set is fixed, so there is no other order to choose; the writer’s reason cites asides (“if I can put it that way”, “of course”, “just”, “!”) that do not occur in this draft, so that reason is generic, but the finding is answered on its merits. E36/E41 heavy second person (12.1 “you” per 100 words) is accepted: four “you” in 33 words, each being the person who says the word or is asked (the replaced sentences had about 10 per 100), the whole paragraph addresses the reader, and these lines say what each word does rather than coaching or validating. O30 (“you say” three times) is accepted: the repeat does a job, since each “If you say” introduces a different word of the set of three, which is what the reader needs to find and remember, and the replaced sentences already repeated “say” for each word.
